headline: Verifiable equivalence across languages and platforms in bioinformatics software
label: Reproducible Bioinformatics Tool Infrastructure
summary: Recent preprints and publications address interoperability and verifiable reproduction of genomic analysis software across languages and platforms.
synthesis: The common thread is portability and reproducibility of analysis software: methods and data structures are re-implemented or exchanged so that they behave consistently across languages and platforms. BiocPy provides Python packages mirroring Bioconductor genomic data structures, with lossless R (.rds) and ArtifactDB exchange and shared C++ methods across R and Python. The St. Nicolas House Analysis case study transpiles one Fusion implementation into nine languages and reports identical outputs. Other items extend this toolkit landscape without sharing the same focus: BRISANCE, a GPU-accelerated Parabricks pipeline for somatic variant calling, is compared against DRAGEN and reports a 20.6-fold speedup, while pyGENIE, Met4All and snputils provide Python and R access layers for cancer genomics, methylation arrays and population genetics. What is new is the explicit emphasis on verifiable equivalence across implementations and execution environments.
